skill.name: ascii-visualizer
skill.description: Creates ASCII diagrams for plans, architectures, workflows, comparisons, metrics, and file structures. Use it when a visual text diagram can make technical information easier to understand.
skill.summary: Turns technical plans and system explanations into readable ASCII visualizations.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

content.value_statement: Technical plans can become hard to scan when they are only prose. This skill turns architectures, workflows, comparisons, and metrics into readable ASCII diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Creates ASCII box diagrams for components and relationships.
Formats file trees and folder hierarchies with labels.
Builds flow charts for workflows and data movement.
Creates comparison tables for before and after states.
Shows progress bars and metric summaries in text form.
Provides a reference set of box-drawing characters and status symbols.
limitations: It produces text diagrams only, not image files or vector graphics.
Complex diagrams may need manual tightening for narrow terminals.
It does not validate live architecture or inspect project files by itself.
It is not intended for code syntax highlighting or Markdown tables.

use_cases.title: Explain a System Architecture
use_cases.description: Show services, folders, integrations, and data flow in a compact text diagram.

use_cases.title: Present an Implementation Plan
use_cases.description: Turn phases, ownership, dependencies, and progress into a readable workflow view.

use_cases.title: Document Project Structure
use_cases.description: Create file-tree diagrams that help contributors understand where features and shared code live.

prompt_templates.title: Show a Simple Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small workflow diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Visualize this workflow as a simple ASCII flow chart: user submits a form, the API validates it, and the database stores it.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Folder Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Organize a project layout for documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASCII file tree for this project structure and add short labels for each major folder.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an ASCII comparison view for these two architecture options, including complexity, cost, reliability, and migration effort.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Layered Architecture Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete technical explanation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a layered ASCII architecture diagram with service boundaries, data flow, implementation phases, risks, and progress indicators.

output_examples.input: A request to explain a web app architecture with frontend, API, services, and storage.
output_examples.output: A compact component diagram that shows each layer, arrows between systems, and short notes for each responsibility.

output_examples.input: A request to compare an old folder layout with a simplified new layout.
output_examples.output: A before-and-after text table that highlights folder count, complexity, type safety, and expected maintenance impact.

output_examples.input: A request to show implementation progress across four dashboard tabs.
output_examples.output: A progress summary with labeled bars, completion percentages, status markers, and a short milestone list.

best_practices: Provide the main entities, relationships, and audience before asking for a diagram.
Ask for compact output when the diagram must fit in terminals or pull requests.
Use labels for responsibilities, risks, and status so the diagram stands alone.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for large raw code blocks or syntax highlighting.
Do not request dense diagrams that must show every low-level detail at once.
Do not rely on generated diagrams as proof that the real system matches the design.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates ASCII diagrams for architectures, workflows, plans, comparisons, metrics, and file structures.

faq.question: Does it generate images?
faq.answer: No. It generates text diagrams that can be pasted into issues, pull requests, documents, and chat.

faq.question: Can it inspect my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It visualizes information supplied in the prompt or gathered by the host assistant through normal tools.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: It includes box diagrams, file trees, flow charts, comparison tables, progress bars, and character references.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when you need precise rendered graphics, formal modeling notation, or direct code syntax formatting.
